component FileSupport
export FileSupport

(***********************************************************
 * Types to support file input and output
 ***********************************************************)

trait Closeable
    close():()
end

trait FileStream extends Closeable
    getter fileName():String
end

trait Consumable
    consume():()
    whenUnconsumed():()
end

trait ReadStream extends { Closeable, Consumable }
    (** eof returns true if an end-of-file condition has been
        encountered on the stream.
     **)
    getter eof():Boolean

    (** ready returns true if there is currently input from the stream
        available to be consumed.
     **)
    getter ready():Boolean

    (** Returns the next available line from the stream, discarding
        line termination characters.  Returns "" on eof.
     **)
    readLine():String = do whenUnconsumed(); uncheckedReadLine() end

    (** Returns the next available character from the stream, or %char(0)% on eof.
     **)
    readChar():Char = do whenUnconsumed(); eofCheckedReadChar() end

    (** Returns the next k characters from the stream.  It will block
        until at least one character is available, and will then
        return as many characters as are ready.  Will return "" on end
        of file.  If k<=0 or absent a default value is chosen.
     **)
    read(k:ZZ32):String = do whenUnconsumed(); uncheckedRead(k) end

    read():String = read(0)

    uncheckedReadLine():String

    uncheckedReadChar():ZZ32

    eofCheckedReadChar():ZZ32 = do
        r = uncheckedReadChar()
        if r = -1 then char(0) else char(r) end
      end

    uncheckedRead(k:ZZ32):String

    (** All file generators yield file contents in parallel by
        default, with a natural ordering corresponding to the order
        data occurs in the underlying file.  The file is closed if all
        its contents have been read.

        These generators pull in multiple chunks of data (where a
        "chunk" is a line, a character, or a block) before it is
        processed.  The maximum number of chunks to pull in before
        processing is given by the last optional argument in every
        case; if it is <=0 or absent a default value is chosen.

        It is possible to read from a ReadStream before invoking any
        of the following methods.  Previously-read data is ignored,
        and only the remaining data is provided by the generator.

        At the moment it is illegal to read from a ReadStream once any
        of these methods has been called; we do not check for this
        condition.  However, the sequential versions of these
        generators may use label/exit or throw in order to escape from
        a loop, and the ReadStream will remain open and ready for
        reading.

        Once the ReadStream has been completely consumed it is closed.
     **)


    (** lines yields the lines found in the file a la readLine().
     **)
    lines(n:ZZ32):Generator[\String\] = do
        consume()
        FileGenerator[\String\](self, n,
            fn (r:ReadStream): Maybe[\String\] => do
               s = r.uncheckedReadLine()
               (if |s| = 0 AND: r.eof() then Nothing[\String\] else Just s)
            end)
      end
    lines():Generator[\String\] = lines(0)

    (** characters yields the characters found in the file a la %readChar()%.
     **)
    characters(n:ZZ32):Generator[\Char\] = do
        consume()
        FileGenerator[\Char\](self, n,
            fn (r:ReadStream): Maybe[\Char\] => do
               c = r.uncheckedReadChar()
               (if c = -1 then Nothing[\Char\] else Just char(c) )
            end)
      end
    characters():Generator[\Char\] = characters(0)

    (** chunks returns chunks of characters found in the file, in the
        sense of read().  The first argument is equivalent to the
        argument k to read, the second (if present) is the number of
        chunks at a time.
     **)
    chunks(n:ZZ32,m:ZZ32):Generator[\String\] = do
        consume()
        FileGenerator[\String\](self, m,
            fn (r:ReadStream): Maybe[\String\] => (if r.eof() then Nothing[\String\] else Just r.uncheckedRead(n)))
      end
    chunks(n:ZZ32): Generator[\String\] = chunks(n,0)
    chunks(): Generator[\String\] = chunks(0,0)
end

(** A FileGenerator generates values from the contents of a
    ReadStream.  Unlike other generators its contents can be consumed
    exactly once.

    A FileGenerator generates file contents in parallel in chunks.
    These chunks get larger as we proceed through the file, until we
    reach some upper bound on the number of chunks being consumed at
    once.  This upper bound is specified by upper, except that
    meaningless values of upper <= 0 are replaced by the default value
    of 1024.
 **)
object FileGenerator[\S\](reader:ReadStream, upper: ZZ32,
                          readOne:ReadStream -> Maybe[\S\])
        extends { Consumable, Generator[\S\] }
    consumed : Boolean := false
    up : ZZ32 = if upper <= 0 then 1024 else upper end
    consume():() = atomic do whenUnconsumed(); consumed := true end
    whenUnconsumed():() =
        if consumed then
            fail("Using consumed generator of " reader)
        end
    generate[\R\](r: Reduction[\R\], body: S->R): R = do
        consume()
        go(n:ZZ32): R =
            if reader.eof() then r.empty()
            else
                (* First read must block, and not check reader.ready() *)

                    i := 1

                    end
                end

            end
        a = go(8 MIN up)
        reader.close()
        a

(* The writer side: stdOut, stdErr, a file Writer and a BufferedWriter write and name themselves, and a missing file raises FileNotFoundException. *)
component NativeHelperWriterWalk
import File.{...}
import Writer.{...}
export Executable

fileLines(name: String): String = do
  r = FileReadStream(name)
  acc: String := ""
  while NOT r.eof do
    acc := acc || "[" || r.readLine() || "]"
  end
  r.close()
  acc
end

run():() = do
  println("1 println of a literal")
  println("2 non-ASCII through println: héllo λ → ∑")
  stdOut.write("3 stdOut.write of a flat string")
  stdOut.write('!')
  stdOut.write('\n')
  rope = "4 a rope: abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz" || "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ" || "\n"
  assert(rope.depth > 0, true, "the rope is not flat")
  stdOut.write(rope)
  stdOut.flush()
  assert(stdOut.asString, "Writer on \"<stdout>\"", "stdOut.asString")
  assert(stdOut.fileName, "<stdout>", "stdOut.fileName")
  stdErr.write("5 stdErr.write, on the error stream\n")
  stdErr.flush()
  assert(stdErr.asString, "Writer on \"<stderr>\"", "stdErr.asString")
  assert(stdErr.fileName, "<stderr>", "stdErr.fileName")

  name = "NativeHelperWriterWalk.out"
  w = Writer(name)
  assert(w.fileName, name, "a file Writer's fileName")
  assert(w.asString, "Writer on \"NativeHelperWriterWalk.out\"", "a file Writer's asString")
  w.write("line one\n")
  w.write('x')
  w.write('\n')
  w.write("a rope in a file: abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz" || "0123456789" || "\n")
  w.flush()
  b = BufferedWriter(w, 8)
  assert(b.asString, "BufferedWriter on Writer on \"NativeHelperWriterWalk.out\"", "BufferedWriter's asString")
  b.write("buffered through a BufferedWriter of size 8\n")
  b.write('y')
  b.flush()
  b.close()
  assert(fileLines(name),
         "[line one][x][a rope in a file: abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789][buffered through a BufferedWriter of size 8][y][]",
         "the file's contents")

  caught: String := "nothing"
  try
    m = Writer("no-such-dir-NativeHelperWriterWalk/missing.txt")
    m.close()
  catch e
    FileNotFoundException => caught := "FileNotFoundException"
  end
  assert(caught, "FileNotFoundException", "a missing file")
  println("6 the writer side wrote and named itself")
end

end

(* On the compiled path, the fileOps helpers of the writer side, the standard streams' among them, compile and run when bound over the JavaBufferedWriter that the compile reads. *)
component NativeHelperFamilyWriterCompiled
export Executable

wOpen(name:JavaString):JavaBufferedWriter = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbwOpen")
wStdOut():JavaBufferedWriter = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbwStdOut")
wStdErr():JavaBufferedWriter = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbwStdErr")
wString(w:JavaBufferedWriter, s:JavaString):() = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbwWriteString")
wChar(w:JavaBufferedWriter, c:ZZ32):() = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbwWriteChar")
wFlush(w:JavaBufferedWriter):() = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbwFlush")
wClose(w:JavaBufferedWriter):() = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbwClose")

run():() = do
  name = "NativeHelperFamilyWriterCompiled.out"
  f = wOpen(name.asJavaString)
  wString(f, "line one".asJavaString)
  wChar(f, 10)
  wChar(f, 120)
  wChar(f, 10)
  wFlush(f)
  wString(f, "after the flush".asJavaString)
  wClose(f)
  r = makeJavaBufferedReader(name)

  wFlush(e)
  o = wStdOut()

  wChar(o, 10)
  wFlush(o)
end

shouldBeTheSame(a:String, b:String, diag:String,f:String):() =

streamTest(s:String, inter:String, op: ReadStream -> String, desc:String) = do
    println("************************* " desc)
    rs = FileReadStream("testFile.txt")
    res : String := op(rs)
    while NOT (rs.eof()) do

    end
    rs.close()
    shouldBeTheSame(s,res,"ReadStream using ",desc)

genTest[\S\](s:String, inter:String, gen: ReadStream -> Generator[\S\], desc: String) = do
    println("************************* par " desc)
    rs = FileReadStream("testFile.txt")
    res = BIG ||[l<-gen(rs)] l inter
    rs.close()
    shouldBeTheSame(s,res,"Generated using ",desc)
    println("************************* seq " desc)
    rss = FileReadStream("testFile.txt")
    ress : String := ""
    for l <- seq(gen(rss)) do
        ress := ress l inter
    end
    rss.close()
    shouldBeTheSame(s,ress,"Generated sequentially using ",desc)
    println("************************* seq gen " desc)
    rs3 = FileReadStream("testFile.txt")
    res3 = BIG ||[l <- seq(gen(rs3))] l inter

  end

      s0 = "Writing into a file..."//
      s1 = "Writing again..."//
      s2 = "And an unterminated line."
      s = s0 s1 s2
      fout.write(s0)
      fout.write(s1)
      fout.write(s2)
      if closeit then fout.close() else fout.flush() end
      s
  end

component Stream
import FlatString.FlatString
export Stream
(***********************************************************
 * Types to support input and output
 ***********************************************************)
trait Closeable
    close():()
end
trait FileStream extends Closeable
    getter fileName():String
end
trait Consumable
    consume():()
    whenUnconsumed():()
end
trait WriteStream extends { Closeable }
    (** %write(FlatString)% and %write(Char)% are the primitive mechanisms
        for writing characters to  a %WriteStream%. **)
    abstract write(s: String):()
    abstract write(c: Char):()
    (** %write(Any)% converts its argument to a String using %asString%
        and appends the result to the stream. **)
    write(x: Any):() =
            typecase x of
                x':Object ⇒ write x'.asString
                else   ⇒ write ("" || x)                   (* handles tuples *)
            end
    (** %writes% converts each of the generated elements to a string
        using %asString% unless the element is already a %String% in
        which case it is left alone.  The resulting strings are
        appended together to the end of the stream.  To avoid
        interleaving with concurrent output to the same stream, this
        append step is done monolithically. **)
    writes(x:Generator[\Any\]):() = writes(x,"")
    writes(x: Generator[\Any\], rest: String):() =
        write((BIG ||[e ← x]
                   typecase e of
                        e':String ⇒ e'
                        e':Object ⇒ e'.asString
                        else   ⇒ ("" || e)                 (* handles tuples *)
                   end) || rest)
    (** %print% and %println% convert each of their arguments to a
        string using %asString% unless the element is already a
        %String% in which case it is left alone.  The resulting
        strings are appended together monolithically to the end of the
        stream.  The %println% method also appends a newline.  Both
        then flush the stream. *)
    print(args:Any...): () = do writes(args,""); flush() end
    println(args:Any...): () = do writes(args,"\n"); flush() end
    (** %flush% any output to the stream that is still buffered. **)
    abstract flush():()
    abstract close():()
end WriteStream
end Stream

(* On the compiled path, the nativeHelpers that the string family's bindings name compile and run when bound at the Java types the compile reads, a string as a JavaString and a Char in a ZZ32 code point. *)
component NativeHelperFamilyStringCompiled
export Executable

sLen(s:JavaString):ZZ32 = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleConcatenate.nativeStrlen")
sConcat(a:JavaString, b:JavaString):JavaString = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleConcatenate.nativeConcatenate")
sCmp(a:JavaString, b:JavaString):ZZ32 = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.compareTo")
sCharAt(s:JavaString, i:ZZ32):ZZ32 = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.charAt")
sIndexOf(s:JavaString, c:ZZ32):ZZ32 = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.indexOf")
sExpr(s:JavaString):JavaString = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.asExprString")
sCicmp(a:JavaString, b:JavaString):ZZ32 = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.compareToIgnoreCase")
sSubstr(s:JavaString, lo:ZZ32, hi:ZZ32):JavaString = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.javaSubstr")
sMatches(s:JavaString, m:JavaString):Boolean = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.javaRegExpMatches")
sSplit(s:JavaString, m:JavaString, i:ZZ32):JavaString = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.javaRegExpSplit")
sMatch(regex:JavaString, some:JavaString):Boolean = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.match")
sProperty(name:JavaString, dflt:JavaString):JavaString = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.systemOps.getProperty")
sEnvironment(name:JavaString, dflt:JavaString):JavaString = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.systemOps.getEnvironment")
sLineSeparator():JavaString = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.lineSeparator")
pThreadInfo(s:JavaString):() = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simplePrintln.printThreadInfo")
pWithThread(s:JavaString):() = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simplePrintln.printWithThread")
plnWithThread(s:JavaString):() = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simplePrintln.printlnWithThread")

run():() = do
  e = "".asJavaString
  w = "hello".asJavaString
  abc = "abc".asJavaString
  assert(sLen(e), 0, "nativeStrlen of the empty string")
  assert(sLen(w), 5, "nativeStrlen")
  assert(sConcat("ab".asJavaString, "cd".asJavaString) = "abcd", "nativeConcatenate")
  assert(sConcat(e, w) = "hello", "nativeConcatenate of the empty string")
  assert(sCmp(w, w), 0, "compareTo of equal strings")
  assert(sCmp(abc, "abd".asJavaString), -1, "compareTo below")
  assert(sCmp("a".asJavaString, abc), -2, "compareTo of a prefix")
  assert(sCharAt(w, 0), 104, "charAt(0)")
  assert(sCharAt(w, 4), 111, "charAt(4)")
  assert(sIndexOf(w, 108), 2, "indexOf found")
  assert(sIndexOf(w, 122), -1, "indexOf not found")
  assert(sIndexOf(e, 97), -1, "indexOf in the empty string")
  assert(sExpr("a\"b\\c".asJavaString) = "\"a\\\"b\\\\c\"", "asExprString quotes and escapes")
  assert(sExpr(e) = "\"\"", "asExprString of the empty string")
tests=NativeHelperFamilyStringCompiled
link
run

(* The reader side: a FileWriteStream writes a file, a rope and a flush among it; a FileReadStream and a Reader read it back to its end; a read after consume raises IOFailure and a missing file FileNotFoundException. *)
component NativeHelperReaderWalk
import File.{...}
import FileSupport.{...}
import Reader.{...}
export Executable

linesOf(name: String): ZZ32 = SUM[\ZZ32\][l <- FileReadStream(name).lines()] 1

charactersOf(name: String): ZZ32 = SUM[\ZZ32\][c <- FileReadStream(name).characters()] 1

consumedRead(r: ReadStream): String =
  try
    s = r.readLine()
    "read " || s
  catch e
    IOFailure => "IOFailure"
  end

consumedReader(r: Reader): String =
  try
    r.whenUnconsumed()
    "unconsumed"
  catch e
    IOFailure => "IOFailure"
  end

missingFile(open: String -> Any, name: String): String =
  try
    ignore(open(name))
    "opened"
  catch e
    FileNotFoundException => "FileNotFoundException"
  end

run():() = do
  name = "NativeHelperReaderWalk.out"
  w = FileWriteStream(name)
  assert(w.fileName, name, "the FileWriteStream's fileName")
  assert(w.asString, "<Write handle to \"NativeHelperReaderWalk.out\">", "the FileWriteStream's asString")
  w.write("alpha\n")
  w.write('b')
  w.write('\n')
  rope = "a rope in a file: abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz" || "0123456789" || "\n"
  assert(rope.depth > 0, true, "the rope is not flat")
  w.write(rope)
  w.flush()
  early = FileReadStream(name)
  assert(early.readLine(), "alpha", "the first line, read after the flush and before the close")
  early.close()
  w.write("gamma")
  w.write("\ndelta\n")
  w.close()

  r = FileReadStream(name)
  assert(r.fileName, name, "the FileReadStream's fileName")
  assert(r.asString, "<Read handle to \"NativeHelperReaderWalk.out\">", "the FileReadStream's asString")
  assert(r.eof, false, "eof at the start")
  assert(r.ready, true, "ready at the start")
  assert(r.readLine(), "alpha", "readLine")
  assert(r.readChar(), 'b', "readChar")
  assert(r.readLine(), "", "readLine of the rest of a line")
  assert(r.read(5), "a rop", "read(5)")
  assert(r.readLine(), "e in a file: abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789", "readLine of the rope's line")
  assert(r.readLine(), "gamma", "readLine of gamma")
  assert(r.readLine(), "delta", "readLine of the last line")
  assert(r.eof, false, "eof before the end is read")
  assert(r.readLine(), "", "readLine at the end")
  assert(r.eof, true, "eof at the end")
  assert(r.uncheckedReadChar(), -1, "uncheckedReadChar at the end")
  assert(r.readChar(), char(0), "readChar at the end")
  assert(r.read(4), "", "read(4) at the end")
  r.close()
  assert(r.eof, true, "eof after the close")

  assert(linesOf(name), 5, "lines() counted")
  assert(charactersOf(name), |"alpha\n"| + 2 + |rope| + |"gamma"| + |"\ndelta\n"|, "characters() counted")

  c = FileReadStream(name)
  ignore(c.lines())
  assert(consumedRead(c), "IOFailure", "a read after consume")
  c.close()

  rd = Reader(name)
  assert(rd.fileName, name, "the Reader's fileName")
  assert(rd.asString, "Reader on \"NativeHelperReaderWalk.out\"", "the Reader's asString")
  assert(rd.eof, false, "a Reader's eof at the start")
  assert(rd.isReady, true, "a Reader's isReady at the start")
  assert(rd.uncheckedReadChar(), 97, "a Reader's uncheckedReadChar")
  assert(rd.uncheckedReadLine(), "lpha", "a Reader's uncheckedReadLine")
  assert(rd.uncheckedRead(4), "b\na ", "a Reader's uncheckedRead(4)")
  assert(consumedReader(rd), "unconsumed", "a Reader before consume")
  rd.consume()
  assert(consumedReader(rd), "IOFailure", "a Reader after consume")
  rd.close()
  assert(rd.eof, true, "a Reader's eof after the close")

  rd2 = Reader(name)
  n: ZZ32 := 0
  while NOT rd2.eof do
    ignore(rd2.uncheckedReadLine())
    n += 1
  end
  assert(n, 6, "a Reader's lines to its end")
  assert(rd2.uncheckedReadChar(), -1, "a Reader's uncheckedReadChar at the end")
  assert(rd2.uncheckedRead(3), "", "a Reader's uncheckedRead(3) at the end")
  rd2.close()

  assert(stdIn.fileName, "<stdin>", "stdIn's fileName")
  assert(stdIn.asString, "Reader on \"<stdin>\"", "stdIn's asString")

  missing = "no-such-dir-NativeHelperReaderWalk/missing.txt"
  assert(missingFile(fn (s: String): Any => FileReadStream(s), missing), "FileNotFoundException", "a FileReadStream on a missing file")
  assert(missingFile(fn (s: String): Any => Reader(s), missing), "FileNotFoundException", "a Reader on a missing file")
  assert(missingFile(fn (s: String): Any => FileWriteStream(s), missing), "FileNotFoundException", "a FileWriteStream in a missing folder")
  println("the reader side read its file back")
end

end
EOF

(* On the compiled path, the fileOps helpers of the reader side, the standard input's among them, compile and run when bound over the JavaBufferedReader that the compile reads: 0 with eof set at the end, readk, and IOFailure after consume. *)
component NativeHelperFamilyReaderCompiled
export Executable

rOpen(name:JavaString):JavaBufferedReader = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbrOpen")
rStdIn():JavaBufferedReader = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbrStdIn")
rAsString(r:JavaBufferedReader):JavaString = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbrAsString")
rRead(r:JavaBufferedReader):ZZ32 = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbrRead")
rReadLine(r:JavaBufferedReader):JavaString = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbrReadLine")
rReadk(r:JavaBufferedReader, k:ZZ32):JavaString = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbrReadk")
rEof(r:JavaBufferedReader):Boolean = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbrEof")
rReady(r:JavaBufferedReader):Boolean = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbrReady")
rClose(r:JavaBufferedReader):() = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbrClose")
rWhenUnconsumed(r:JavaBufferedReader):() = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbrWhenUnconsumed")
rConsume(r:JavaBufferedReader):() = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbrConsume")

refusedAfterConsume(r:JavaBufferedReader):Boolean =
  try
    rWhenUnconsumed(r)
    false
  catch e
    IOFailure => true
  end

run():() = do
  name = "NativeHelperFamilyReaderCompiled.out"
  w = makeJavaBufferedWriter(name)
  w.write("alpha\nbeta\nxy")

  assert(NOT rEof(r), "eof at the start")

  assert(rReadLine(r) = "", "jbrReadLine of the rest of a line")

component NativeHelperFamilyReaderCompiled
export Executable

rOpen(name:JavaString):JavaBufferedReader = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbrOpen")
rStdIn():JavaBufferedReader = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbrStdIn")
rAsString(r:JavaBufferedReader):JavaString = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbrAsString")
rRead(r:JavaBufferedReader):ZZ32 = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbrRead")
rReadLine(r:JavaBufferedReader):JavaString = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbrReadLine")
rReadk(r:JavaBufferedReader, k:ZZ32):JavaString = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbrReadk")
rEof(r:JavaBufferedReader):Boolean = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbrEof")
rReady(r:JavaBufferedReader):Boolean = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbrReady")
rClose(r:JavaBufferedReader):() = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbrClose")
rWhenUnconsumed(r:JavaBufferedReader):() = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbrWhenUnconsumed")
rConsume(r:JavaBufferedReader):() = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbrConsume")

refusedAfterConsume(r:JavaBufferedReader):Boolean =
  try
    rWhenUnconsumed(r)
    false
  catch e
    IOFailure => true
  end

run():() = do
  name = "NativeHelperFamilyReaderCompiled.out"
  w = makeJavaBufferedWriter(name)
  w.write("alpha\nbeta\nxy")
  w.close()
  r = rOpen(name.asJavaString)
  assert(rAsString(r) = "[buffered reader [Buffered reader NativeHelperFamilyReaderCompiled.out]]", "jbrAsString names the file")
  assert(NOT rEof(r), "eof at the start")
  assert(rReady(r), "ready at the start")
  assert(rReadLine(r) = "alpha", "jbrReadLine")
  assert(rRead(r), 98, "jbrRead answers the code point")
  assert(rReadk(r, 3) = "eta", "jbrReadk")
  assert(rReadLine(r) = "", "jbrReadLine of the rest of a line")
  assert(rReadk(r, 0) = "xy", "jbrReadk with no count reads what remains")
  assert(NOT rEof(r), "eof before the end is read")
  assert(rRead(r), 0, "jbrRead at the end answers 0")
  assert(rEof(r), "eof is set at the end")
  assert(rReadLine(r) = "", "jbrReadLine at the end")
  assert(rReadk(r, 4) = "", "jbrReadk at the end")
  rClose(r)
  c = rOpen(name.asJavaString)
  rWhenUnconsumed(c)
  assert(NOT refusedAfterConsume(c), "a reader before consume")
  rConsume(c)
  assert(refusedAfterConsume(c), "a reader after consume raises IOFailure")
  rClose(c)
  i = rStdIn()
  assert(rAsString(i) = "[buffered reader [Buffered reader <stdin>]]", "jbrStdIn names the standard input")
  assert(NOT rEof(i), "the standard input before a read")
  println("PASS")
end

end
EOF

\item[Effect] 341 of the 443 bindings of \library\ name a helper:
the operators \EXP{=}, \EXP{<}, the prefix and infix \EXP{-} and
\EXP{\dotminus}, \EXP{+}, \EXP{\dotplus}, \EXP{\cdot}, \EXP{\times},
juxtaposition, \EXP{\dottimes}, \EXP{\div}, \OPR{REM}, \OPR{MOD}, \OPR{GCD},
\OPR{LCM}, \OPR{BITAND}, \OPR{BITOR}, \OPR{BITXOR}, \OPR{BITNOT} and
\OPR{CHOOSE} of the traits \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} and \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}, with the
functions \VAR{widen}, \VAR{unsigned} and \VAR{partitionL} of the first and
\VAR{narrow}, \VAR{unsigned}, \VAR{big} and \VAR{partitionL} of the second, and
the same operators but \EXP{<} of the trait \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, with its
\VAR{cmp}; the shifts \OPR{LSHIFT} and \OPR{RSHIFT} and the power of these
three traits, of the trait \EXP{\mathbb{N}64} and of the interpreter's object
\EXP{\mathbb{N}32}, with the \VAR{shift} of \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, each bound at a
count or exponent of type \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} or \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} beside a
declaration over \TYP{AnyIntegral} that converts its count or exponent and calls
it; twenty-eight bindings of the trait \EXP{\mathbb{N}64}, and of the
interpreter's objects thirty-one of \EXP{\mathbb{N}32}, three of
\TYP{UnsignedLong}, forty-one of \TYP{Char}, sixty-two of \TYP{Float} and
fifty-one of \EXP{\mathbb{R}32}; the getters \VAR{asString}, \VAR{asExprString}
and \VAR{asFloat} of the interpreter's objects \TYP{Int}, \TYP{Long} and
\TYP{BigNum}; the thirteen methods of the object \TYP{FlatString} of \library\
and its line separator; the method \VAR{ilkName} of the trait \TYP{Object} and
\EXP{\sequiv} over \TYP{Any}; the four methods of the trait
\TYP{JavaBufferedWriter} and its three factories, over a file's name, standard
output and standard error; and the functions \VAR{char}, \VAR{fromRawBits},
\VAR{nanoTime}, \VAR{random} and \VAR{match}, with \VAR{printThreadInfo},
\VAR{printWithThread}, \VAR{printlnWithThread}, \VAR{getEnvironment} and
\VAR{getProperty}, each of these five declared over \TYP{FlatString} beside an
overload over \TYP{String} that flattens its argument, and \VAR{match} beside
one over two \TYP{String}s that flattens both.
Two of the helpers named, \texttt{stringOps.typeName} for the method
\VAR{ilkName} of the trait \TYP{Object} and \texttt{equality.sEquiv} for
\EXP{\sequiv} over \TYP{Any}, the interpreter does not load: it answers each
with an operation of its own, and the compiled code calls the helper.
The other 102 still name a glue class, which the compiled code cannot call.
Until the compiled code moves onto \library, the type checker checks the moved
bindings, but no compiled program runs them.
Where a binding declares \EXP{\mathbb{N}32}, \EXP{\mathbb{N}64} or \TYP{Char}
at a position at which its helper takes or answers a Java \texttt{int} or
\texttt{long}, or \TYP{UnsignedLong}, the interpreter's object of
\EXP{\mathbb{N}64}, at an argument, the compiler composes the call with one of six transfer helpers
at that position, as the compiled library writes its own operations on those
types, and the type checker checks the composition.
Under the interpreter a helper's raise of \TYP{IntegerOverflow} or
\TYP{DivisionByZero} is the library's own exception, so \EXP{\div}, \OPR{REM} and \OPR{MOD} by zero on \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32},
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, \EXP{\mathbb{N}32} and
\EXP{\mathbb{N}64} throw a \TYP{DivisionByZero}, as \chapref{operators} says

The interpreter refuses at load a helper bound with a parameter declared

No binding of \library\ takes a parameter declared \TYP{String}.

run():() = do
  name = "NativeHelperFamilyReaderCompiled.out"
  w = makeJavaBufferedWriter(name)
  w.write("alpha\nbeta\nxy")
  w.close()
  r = rOpen(name.asJavaString)
  assert(rAsString(r) = "[buffered reader [Buffered reader NativeHelperFamilyReaderCompiled.out]]", "jbrAsString names the file")
  assert(NOT rEof(r), "eof at the start")
  assert(rReady(r), "ready at the start")
  assert(rReadLine(r) = "alpha", "jbrReadLine")
  assert(rRead(r), 98, "jbrRead answers the code point")
  assert(rReadk(r, 3) = "eta", "jbrReadk")
  assert(rReadLine(r) = "", "jbrReadLine of the rest of a line")
  assert(rReadk(r, 0) = "xy", "jbrReadk with no count reads what remains")
  assert(NOT rEof(r), "eof before the end is read")
  assert(rRead(r), 0, "jbrRead at the end answers 0")
  assert(rEof(r), "eof is set at the end")
  assert(rReadLine(r) = "", "jbrReadLine at the end")
  assert(rReadk(r, 4) = "", "jbrReadk at the end")
  rClose(r)
  c = rOpen(name.asJavaString)
  rWhenUnconsumed(c)
  rConsume(c)
  assert(rReadLine(c) = "alpha", "jbrReadLine after consume")
  rClose(c)
  assert(rEof(c), "eof after the close")
  i = rStdIn()
  assert(rAsString(i) = "[buffered reader [Buffered reader <stdin>]]", "jbrStdIn names the standard input")
  assert(NOT rEof(i), "the standard input before a read")
  println("PASS")
end

== explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md, ## 3. Traits, objects and components
fortress-gap-ledger.md:340
| # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 928 | under walk, a program's object that extends `JavaBufferedWriter` loads, and its first call of an inherited `write`, `flush` or `close` stops, since those are natives over a Java writer and the trait has no `comprises` clause to name its private native object | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | design limit (library) | silent | none | climb batch 27 rung W's skeptic | siblings: 551. The trait (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1948-1957`) has no `comprises` clause, unlike `ZZ32`'s `comprises { Int }` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:553`), since its native object `JavaBufferedWriterObject` is private to `FortressBuiltin` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:790`); the loader's `unbox` refuses any other value (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/StaticNativeApp.java:292-295`). Probe `object Fake extends JavaBufferedWriter end` with `Fake.write("x")`: 'No Java FortressBufferedWriter carries Fake', rc=1; on the base, 'JavaBufferedWriter is undefined.'. Workaround: a program's own writer extends `WriteStream`. |
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The gap ledger's tool: it owns the ledger's format, reads its rows, and is
the only way to write them.

The ledger, explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md, is sorted into topic sections,
each a "## TITLE" heading over one table of rows. A row is one line of eight
cells, and keeps its number wherever it sits:

  | # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |

The template (POSITIONS.md, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is
explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md, 4.1):
  status       exactly one of POSITIVE-VERIFIED, NEGATIVE-VERIFIED,
               NEGATIVE-BOUNDED, CONTESTED, RETIRED, FIXED, DUPLICATE
  class        `kind (area)`, kind one of the legend's seven, area one of ten;
               `—` only for POSITIVE-VERIFIED and RETIRED
  spec         the .tex file and the section heading in quotes; a line number
               only against Specification-1.0-frozen/; `silent` where the
               specification does not say
  reproducer   one test (a name under the test folders, or a path) or probe
               path from the repository root, or `none`
  limits       row 1,200 characters, claim 300, reproducer 200, found by 60,
               notes 700
  a pipe inside a cell is written \\|

Cells are split only at a pipe that is not escaped as \\|. A row whose cells
hold bare pipes (the ledger had six) does not split into its table's width that
way; it is read by its split at pipes followed by a space or the line's end, as
facts-extract.py has always read it, and check reports it under `pipe`.

Every write takes a lock (flock on .ledger.lock beside the ledger), checks the
template on the line it writes, and puts the full earlier line of a row it
changes, unchanged, in the history file beside the ledger
(fortress-gap-ledger-history.md), under "### Row N" and a line saying what
became of it. A failed check prints the rules the row breaks and exits 1.
add, rewrite, close and duplicate check the whole line they write; note checks
only what it changes (the notes cell and the row's length), so that a row
failing the template elsewhere still takes a note. A row at its length limit
takes no note: rewrite cuts it back (the rework's decision D4, "each is cut
when next edited", process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md).

usage: ledger.py COMMAND [ARGS] [--root DIR] [--ledger FILE] [--history FILE]

  heads                      one tab-separated line per row: number, status,
                             class, the claim's first 150 characters, and the
                             paths the row cites in backticks
  sections                   each section that holds a row table: its row
                             count and title, tab-separated
  section TITLE              the heads of that section's rows
  show N [--short]           row N under its section and table header; with
                             --short, its status, class, claim and the notes'
                             first 300 characters
  find WORDS [--open] [--cites FILE[:LINE]] [--all]
                             one line per row that holds every word (whole
                             words, or a word's start with a trailing *):
                             number, status, class, the claim's start; --open
                             leaves out FIXED, DUPLICATE and RETIRED; --cites
                             keeps the rows citing FILE (at LINE) and prints
                             the lines they cite; at most 10 rows unless --all
  count                      the rows by status, kind and area; nothing stored

    set -u
    FH=$PWD ; OUT=$1 ; case "$OUT" in /*) ;; *) OUT="$FH/$OUT" ;; esac ; mkdir -p "$OUT"
    cd "$FH/ProjectFortress/demos"
    LIST=$(ls *.fss | grep -v -E 'Syntax\.fss$|DynamicSemantics\.fss$|Satisfiability\.fss$|GenomeUtil')
    : > "$OUT/summary.tsv"
    for f in $LIST ; do
      n=${f%.fss}
      case "$n" in
        wordcount2) ( cd "$FH" && timeout -k 15 600 bin/fortress ProjectFortress/demos/$f < /dev/null ) > "$OUT/$n.txt" 2>&1 ; rc=$? ;;
        tennisRanking) timeout -k 15 600 ../../bin/fortress $f "$FH/ProjectFortress/demos/tennis050307" "$FH/ProjectFortress/demos/tennis051707" "$FH/ProjectFortress/demos/tennisGames" < /dev/null > "$OUT/$n.txt" 2>&1 ; rc=$? ;;
        *) timeout -k 15 600 ../../bin/fortress $f < /dev/null > "$OUT/$n.txt" 2>&1 ; rc=$? ;;
      esac
      if grep -qi fail "$OUT/$n.txt" ; then fl=fail-in-output ; else fl=clean ; fi
      if [ $rc -eq 0 ] && [ $fl = clean ] ; then v=END ; elif [ $rc -eq 124 ] || [ $rc -eq 137 ] ; then v=LIMIT ; else v=STOP ; fi

== explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:7-27

## The row template

A row is one line of eight cells, `| # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |`, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of its topic section, in number order. A pipe inside a cell is written `\|`. (POSITIONS, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md`, section 4.)

- **#**: the row's number, the next free one when it is added; never reused, renumbered or given to another row. 148 is vacant.
- **claim**: at most 300 characters, whose first 150 name the defect or the capability: what fails or what holds, and where.
- **status**: exactly one word of seven, with no second status and nothing in brackets:
  - `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`: it works; it ran and its output is recorded.
  - `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`: the specification settles it and the reproducer confirms it. A row with one half fixed stays `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, and its notes say which half is fixed.
  - `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`: the failure reproduces; the mechanisms tried are named and are not exhaustive.
  - `CONTESTED`: unsettled; the notes say why.
  - `RETIRED`: a source's claim falsified here, kept so that it is not derived again.
  - `FIXED`: closed by a landed commit (`ledger.py close`): the claim's first sentence, the test as reproducer, notes `fixed HASH; full text: history, row N`.
  - `DUPLICATE`: a pointer (`ledger.py duplicate`), notes `duplicate of row M; full text: history, row N`.
- **class**: `kind (area)`; `—` only for `POSITIVE-VERIFIED` and `RETIRED`. The kind is one of `implementation gap`, `library gap vs spec`, `library bug`, `design limit`, `deliberate`, `typesetter`, `packaging`; the area one of `parser`, `walk`, `checker`, `codegen`, `runtime`, `library`, `prelude`, `specification`, `tests`, `tools`.
- **spec citation**: the `.tex` file and the section heading in quotes, as `basic/operators/juxtameaning.tex`, "Juxtaposition"; a line number only against `Specification-1.0-frozen/`; `silent` where the specification does not say.
- **reproducer**: one test (its name, or its path under the test folders; an `XXX` test while it is an expected failure) or one probe path from the repository root, at most 200 characters; `none` when nothing in the tree reproduces it, with the command and its output, or the probe's old path, in the notes.
- **found by**: the stream that found it (`climb batch 8 rung I`, `run-c3`, `apl rung 2`), at most 60 characters; no date and no role.
- **notes / workaround**: at most 700 characters: `siblings: N, M` first if there are any; the mechanism, with file:line and the commit it was true at; the workaround; for a closed row, `fixed HASH`.

A path under `explorations/` that is no longer in the tree is read from history: `git show $(git log -1 --diff-filter=D --format=%h -- PATH)^:PATH`.

## B.12 Native code and Java interop

The two worlds bind native code by two mechanisms that share nothing but the word "native".

Interpreter: a function whose body is literally `builtinPrimitive("some.java.Class")` is pattern-matched in `NativeApp.checkAndLoadNative` (`interpreter/glue/NativeApp.java:164-229`). A string under `com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.` names a static Java method, `"com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.Class.method"`: `interpreter/glue/StaticNativeApp.java` takes, among the class's public static methods of 

There are 231 such bindings in `LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss`, 108 in `Library/FortressLibrary.fss` and 7 in `LibraryBuiltin/NativeArray.fss`.

Compiler: a `.fss` writes `import java com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.{class.method => name, …}` (16 such lines in `LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss`, 3 in `Library/CompilerLibrary.fss`); `ForeignJava` reads the Java class with ASM to synthesize an api for it (`repository/ForeignJava.java:132-136,565-575`), and `FortressTransformer` rewrites the class into a wrapper whose methods take and retu

`import java` also works on the interpreter path, by a third route that is easy to miss: `ForeignComponentWrapper` populates an environment from `ForeignJava`'s synthesized declarations (`interpreter/env/ForeignComponentWrapper.java:59`), and `ClosureMaker` generates, at run time, a `NativeFn<n>` subclass that calls the Java method and writes it into `bytecode_cache` (`interpreter/env/ClosureMaker

No test under `ProjectFortress/tests/` uses `import java` (0 files), while 2 under `compiler_tests/` do, so the interpreter's foreign-Java route is present but not exercised by the gated suite.

There is no way for a Fortress program to be called *from* Java other than by loading the generated classes through `InstantiatingClassloader`, which is what `MainWrapper` does.

Meaning: a program that stopped on walk's error now stops on the exception's name or catches it (fork R6); one that read after `close` now reads the end.

Holds on the base and on the edit: `compiler_tests/XXXFileOpsRaiseCaughtCompiled` (junit.sh: 'REACHED', 'com.sun.fortress.compiler.runtimeValues.FortressImplementationError: fortress.CompilerBuiltin$IOFailure.<init>(java.lang.String)', 'Saw expected failure (Exit code != 0)'), and the probe `tmp/rung-io-reader/cprobe/CompiledMissingProbe.fss`, `makeJavaBufferedReader` of a missing file in a `try` that catches `FileNotFoundException`: 'FortressImplementationError: fortress.CompilerBuiltin$FileNotFoundException.<init>(java.lang.String)', rc=1, old and new. Walk is not hit: there `Class.forName` finds no class, and `StaticNativeApp.raised` raises the library's object. The no-argument form, which `IntegerOverflow` and `DivisionByZero` take, is not hit. **Walk carries `FortressLibrary`'s `JavaBufferedReader` in a Java `FortressBufferedReader`, and `FileReadStream`, `Reader`, `stdIn` and `FileWriteStream` are plain Fortress objects over the two Java-backed traits.** The trait's eight methods and its two factories, over a file name and for standard input, are natives on `nativeHelpers/fileOps` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1959-1979`); walk's loader carries the trait by its name through `FortressBuiltin`'s private native object `JavaBufferedReaderObject` (`interpreter/glue/StaticNativeApp.java:71`). `File` and `Reader` are plain components: each object holds its Java-backed value in its field `under`; `uncheckedReadChar` answers -1 at the end by the reader's `eof`, since `jbrRead` answers 0 there; `FileWriteStream` is a `WriteStream` with its `flush`. Test: `tests/NativeHelperReaderWalk`, `compiler_tests/NativeHelperFamilyReaderCompiled`, `compiler_tests/XXXFileOpsRaiseCaughtCompiled`. - Row 901 closes with `14be0d36`, test `NativeHelperReaderWalk`: `FileWriteStream`'s `flush()` (`Library/File.fss:68`).
- Row 902 closes with `14be0d36`, test `NativeHelperReaderWalk`: a missing file raises `FileNotFoundException` through `FileReadStream`, `Reader` and `FileWriteStream`, which a `catch` sees.

cat tmp/rung-io-reader/row-928.txt
cat <<'EOF'

## New rows

- NEW-R-1, for the section "11. Natives and the run time" or the one that holds row 902's runtime siblings, the gather's choice (linted: only the number rule fails):

EOF
cat tmp/rung-io-reader/row-new.txt
cat <<'EOF'

## Handover line

- **R** (`14be0d36`): Rung R landed P-164's reader side on `wip/rung-io-reader`: `JavaBufferedReader`'s eight natives and two factories on `fileOps` (`jbrStdIn` new), walk's carrier through `JavaBufferedReaderObject`, `FileReadStream`, `Reader`, `stdIn` and `FileWriteStream` (now a `WriteStream` with `flush`) plain objects, `File` and `Reader` plain components; 25 glue bindings go, 10 helper bindings come (351 and 77 of 428); rows 900, 901, 902 and 926 close; on the compiled path a `fileOps` raise is no exception a `catch` sees (NEW-R-1, `XXXFileOpsRaiseCaughtCompiled`); STAGES_LINE.

## Revival change

**The change.** The team's walk library declared `File` and `Reader` as native components whose `FileReadStream`, `FileWriteStream`, `Reader` and `stdIn` are glue objects (base `Library/File.fss:12-81`, `Library/Reader.fss:12-61`): `FileWriteStream` extends only `FileStream` and has no `flush` though its api declares one (base `Library/File.fsi:102`, `:131`), so a rope written to it and its `flush()` stop the run; a missing file, a read after `consume` and a read after `close` stop the run with errors that no `catch` sees ('FileNotFound: …', `interpreter/glue/prim/FileReadStream.java:43-44`; 'Performed operation on consumed FileReadStream …', `:66-70`; 'Read IOException on <Read handle to …>', `:80-89`). The tree now declares `object FileReadStream(fileName: String, under: JavaBufferedReader)`, `object FileWriteStream(fileName: String, under: JavaBufferedWriter) extends { FileStream, WriteStream }` and `object Reader(fileName: String, under: JavaBufferedReader)`, each over a Java-backed value in its field, beside one-argument factories of the old names (`Library/File.fsi:17-19`, `:99-101`; `Library/Reader.fsi:17-19`); `FileWriteStream` takes a rope and flushes; a missing file raises `FileNotFoundException`, a read after `consume` and an I/O error `IOFailure`, both of which a `catch` sees under walk; after `close`, reads answer the end's values (`""`, `char(0)`, -1) and `ready` raises `IOFailure`. The answers after `close` are the team's compiled reader's (`FortressBufferedReader.java:38-40`, `:56-57`, `:73-74`), which returns the end's values once `eof` is set.

**Provenance.** P-164 (option (b) of `explorations/reviews/io-objects-carrier-2026-11-06.md`), with review-queue item 373 for `FileWriteStream`, and forks R1 to R7 of `explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-28.md` at their defaults (R6 for the exceptions, item 384 at its default: they carry no message); climb batch 28, rung R.
EOF

content.content:
# Rung R, climb batch 28: the reader objects over a Java-backed `JavaBufferedReader`, and `File` and `Reader` plain components (P-164)

- problem: every file a program reads goes through `FileReadStream`, an object of the native component `File` whose 10 methods name glue classes that only walk can call (base `Library/File.fss:12-63`), as microGPT's data does (`explorations/run-c4/src/FlatData.fss:69-86`); `Reader` and `stdIn` the same, 10 more (base `Library/Reader.fss:12-61`); `FileWriteStream`'s 5 stayed on glue, a rope stops it and it has no `flush` (rows 926, 900, 901); a missing file stops the run with an error that no `catch` sees (row 902; `explorations/reviews/io-objects-carrier-2026-11-06.md:111-162`).
- spec: none; `grep -rn 'FileReadStream\|FileWriteStream\|JavaBufferedReader\|stdIn' Specification/` prints nothing, and `JavaBufferedWriter` only in Appendix I's natives effect (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:4647`).
- precedent: rung W's writer objects over a field (`Library/Writer.fss:17-36`) and its native object below the trait (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:788-791`, `interpreter/glue/prim/JavaBufferedWriterObject.java`); the team's later `FileReadStream` over a Java reader in a field (`ProjectFortress/BirdyLib/File.fss:20-34`); the prelude's reader trait (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:592-601`).
- deviation: the trait's methods have no `throws` clause, as `JavaBufferedWriter`'s (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1270-1279`); `read()` answers `Char` for the prelude's `Character`, and the streams' `uncheckedReadChar` maps the end's 0 to -1 by `eof` (`Library/File.fss:37-40`, `Library/Reader.fss:37-40`); `FileWriteStream` keeps the team's `write(x:String) = x.writeOn(self)`, `writes`, `print` and `println`, where `Writer` flattens and flushes (`Library/File.fss:57-67`, `Library/Writer.fss:32-35`); the api headers drop the explicit `getter fileName()`, now the value parameter (`Library/File.fsi:19`, `:101`, `Library/Reader.fsi:19`); `File` imports `Stream.{ WriteStream }` by name (`Library/File.fss:15`); the compiled guard leaves the raise after `consume` to an expected failure (NEW-R-1; `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXFileOpsRaiseCaughtCompiled.fss`).
- historical: Library/File.fss, Library/File.fsi, Library/Reader.fss, Library/Reader.fsi, Library/FortressLibrary.fss, Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss, ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/fileOps.java (`interpreter/glue/StaticNativeApp.java` is the revival's; `interpreter/glue/prim/JavaBufferedReaderObject.java` is new).

## What changed and why

Commits on `wip/rung-io-reader`: `f27f6013` (the two tests, failing on the base), `14be0d36` (the change, the compiled guard's final form and the expected failure `XXXFileOpsRaiseCaughtCompiled`), then this report.

- `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1959-1968`, `.fsi:1265-1279`: `trait JavaBufferedReader` gains the prelude's eight methods, each a public native in P-58's form on its `fileOps` helper; `.fss:1976-1979`, `.fsi:1284-1285`: `makeJavaBufferedReader(name: FlatString)` on `jbrOpen` and `makeJavaBufferedStdIn()` on the new `jbrStdIn`, after `makeJavaBufferedStdErr` (fork R4). The api's comment says what the reader answers at the end and after `consume`.
- `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/fileOps.java:96-99`, beside `jbwStdErr`: `public static FortressBufferedReader jbrStdIn()`, a `FortressBufferedReader` named `<stdin>` over a `java.io.BufferedReader` over an `InputStreamReader` of `System.in` in UTF-8, made at each call, as the glue's `inputReader` reads `System.in` in UTF-8 (`interpreter/glue/prim/Reader.java:268-272`, `:57`).
- `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:793-796`, right after `JavaBufferedWriterObject`: `private object JavaBufferedReaderObject extends JavaBufferedReader end`. Its native constructor is the new `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/JavaBufferedReaderObject.java`, rung W's `JavaBufferedWriterObject.java` with the reader's names: it registers itself in its Java constructor, and its nested `Value` holds a `FortressBufferedReader`; the singleton that walk makes holds none and no helper is passed it.
- `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/StaticNativeApp.java`, four methods: `javaFor` carries `JavaBufferedReader` by name in `FortressBufferedReader` (`:71`, its comment `:55-58`), `carried` admits that class (`:104`), `unbox` takes the reader out of a `JavaBufferedReaderObject.Value` (`:300-303`), `box` makes one (`:327`); two imports (`:4`, `:13`). `javaForSelf(String)` falls through to `javaFor`, unchanged.
- `Library/File.fss` and `.fsi`: `component File`, no longer native, and without the glue's `language` and `package`. `object FileReadStream(fileName: String, under: JavaBufferedReader) extends { ReadStream, FileStream }` (`.fss:23-45`): `asString` is the glue's text, `"<Read handle to \"" || fileName || "\">"` (fork R5); `eof`, `ready`, `whenUnconsumed`, `consume`, `uncheckedReadLine`, `uncheckedRead(k)` and `close` call `under`; `uncheckedReadChar` reads `under.read()` and answers -1 where `under.eof()` is then set, else the character's `codePoint` (fork R1), so `ReadStream`'s `eofCheckedReadChar` and `characters` keep the -1 (`Library/FileSupport.fss:64-67`, `:113-118`). Its factory `FileReadStream(filename: String)` (`.fss:18-21`) flattens the name by a `typecase` on `asFlatString` and calls `makeJavaBufferedReader`, as `Writer(fileName)` does (`Library/Writer.fss:20-23`). `object FileWriteStream(fileName: String, under: JavaBufferedWriter) extends { FileStream, WriteStream }` (`.fss:52-70`): its two primitive writes, a new `flush` and `close` call `under`; the team's `write(x:String) = x.writeOn(self)`, `write(x:Any)`, `writes`, `print` and `println` stay as they were; a rope now writes itself on it, since it is a `WriteStream` (rows 900, 901; fork R2). Its factory likewise. `File` imports `Stream.{ WriteStream }`, by name, since `FileSupport` and `Stream` both declare `Closeable`, `FileStream` and `Consumable` (`Library/FileSupport.fsi:18-29`, `Library/Stream.fsi:19-32`).
- `Library/Reader.fss` and `.fsi`: `component Reader`, no longer native, and without its exported `language` and `package` variables. `stdIn: Reader = Reader("<stdin>", makeJavaBufferedStdIn())` (`.fss:17`); the factory `Reader(fileName: String): Reader` (`.fss:19-22`, `.fsi:17`); `object Reader(fileName: String, under: JavaBufferedReader)` (`.fss:24-44`), still outside `ReadStream` as the team left it, with `asString` "Reader on " and the name's `asExprString`, `isReady` on `under.ready()`, and the same `uncheckedReadChar`.
- 25 glue bindings go, all of `File.fss` and `Reader.fss`; 10 helper bindings come, all in `FortressLibrary.fss`. By `tmp/rung-io-reader/count/countbind.py` (comments stripped, the compiler's four files left out): the base build 'helper 341 glue 102 total 443', the edit 'helper 351 glue 77 total 428'. With rung W's 11, P-164's 36 glue bindings are gone. The glue classes stay in the tree, named by no string (fork R3).

### The bindings moved, with their helpers

| binding | before | after | Java signature |
|---|---|---|---|
| a file's reader | the glue constructor `FileReadStream`, `Reader` | `makeJavaBufferedReader(name: FlatString)` | `static FortressBufferedReader jbrOpen(String) throws FException` |
| `stdIn`'s reader | `Reader$inputReader` | `makeJavaBufferedStdIn()` | `static FortressBufferedReader jbrStdIn()` (new) |
| `read(): Char` | `FileReadStream$readChar`, `Reader$readChar` | `JavaBufferedReader.read()` | `static int jbrRead(FortressBufferedReader) throws FException` |
| `readLine(): String` | `…$readLine` | `JavaBufferedReader.readLine()` | `static String jbrReadLine(FortressBufferedReader) throws FException` |
| `readk(k: ZZ32): String` | `…$readk` | `JavaBufferedReader.readk(k)` | `static String jbrReadk(FortressBufferedReader, int) throws FException` |
| `eof(): Boolean` | `…$eof` | `JavaBufferedReader.eof()` | `static boolean jbrEof(FortressBufferedReader)` |
| `ready(): Boolean` | `…$ready` | `JavaBufferedReader.ready()` | `static boolean jbrReady(FortressBufferedReader) throws FException` |
| `close(): ()` | `…$close` | `JavaBufferedReader.close()` | `static void jbrClose(FortressBufferedReader) throws FException` |
| `whenUnconsumed(): ()` | `…$whenUnconsumed` | `JavaBufferedReader.whenUnconsumed()` | `static void jbrWhenUnconsumed(FortressBufferedReader) throws FException` |
| `consume(): ()` | `…$consume` | `JavaBufferedReader.consume()` | `static void jbrConsume(FortressBufferedReader) throws FException` |
| `fileName` (3 objects) | `FileReadStream$fileName`, `FileWriteStream$fileName`, `Reader$fileName` | the value parameter | none |
| `asString` (2 objects) | `FileReadStream$toString`, `FileWriteStream$toString` | Fortress text over `fileName` | none |
| `FileWriteStream`'s `write` twice, `close` | `FileWriteStream$write`, `$close` | `under.write(s)`, `under.write(c)`, `under.close()` on rung W's `jbwWriteString`, `jbwWriteChar`, `jbwClose` | (rung W's) |
| `FileWriteStream.flush()` | none (row 901) | `under.flush()` on `jbwFlush` | (rung W's) |

The methods that became Fortress text: `FileReadStream`'s and `Reader`'s nine each (`asString` of `FileReadStream`, and of both `eof`, `ready`/`isReady`, `whenUnconsumed`, `consume`, `uncheckedReadLine`, `uncheckedReadChar`, `uncheckedRead`, `close`), `FileWriteStream`'s `asString`, two `write`s, `flush` and `close`, the three factories and `stdIn`.

# Rung R, climb batch 28: the record lines

## Findings

1. **The reader side is plain Fortress over a Java-backed `JavaBufferedReader`.** `FortressLibrary`'s `trait JavaBufferedReader` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1959-1968`, `.fsi:1265-1279`) declares the prelude's eight methods (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:592-601`) as public natives on `nativeHelpers/fileOps`: `read(): Char` on `jbrRead`, `readLine` on `jbrReadLine`, `readk(k: ZZ32)` on `jbrReadk`, `eof`, `ready`, `close`, `whenUnconsumed` and `consume` on theirs; the factories `makeJavaBufferedReader(name: FlatString)` on `jbrOpen` and `makeJavaBufferedStdIn()` on the new `fileOps.jbrStdIn` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/fileOps.java:96-99`), a `FortressBufferedReader` over `System.in` in UTF-8 named `<stdin>` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1976-1979`). Walk carries the trait by its name in `FortressBufferedReader` (`interpreter/glue/StaticNativeApp.java:71`, `:104`, `:300-303`, `:327`) through `FortressBuiltin`'s `private object JavaBufferedReaderObject extends JavaBufferedReader` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:793-796`), whose native constructor is the new `interpreter/glue/prim/JavaBufferedReaderObject.java`. `File` and `Reader` are plain components: `object FileReadStream(fileName: String, under: JavaBufferedReader)`, `object FileWriteStream(fileName: String, under: JavaBufferedWriter) extends { FileStream, WriteStream }` (`Library/File.fss:23-45`, `:52-70`) and `object Reader(fileName: String, under: JavaBufferedReader)` (`Library/Reader.fss:24-45`), with `stdIn = Reader("<stdin>", makeJavaBufferedStdIn())` and the one-argument factories, each of which flattens the name by a `typecase` and calls the factory. Holds under walk at the edit `14be0d36`. Evidence: `ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelperReaderWalk.fss` (harness: 'OK (6 tests)' with the four guards), `compiler_tests/NativeHelperFamilyReaderCompiled` (junit.sh: 'OK (6 tests)'). Meaning: no I/O object of the one library names a glue class; P-164's 17 bindings are all on `fileOps`.
2. **The 25 glue bindings of `File` and `Reader` go and 10 helper bindings come: the one library has 428 live bindings, 351 on helpers and 77 on glue classes.** Counted by `tmp/rung-io-reader/count/countbind.py`, comments stripped, the compiler's four files left out: the base build '341 glue 102 total 443' (F-299's and F-32's numbers), the edit 'helper 351 glue 77 total 428'. The 25: `FileReadStream`'s 10 (`fileName`, `toString`, `eof`, `ready`, `whenUnconsumed`, `consume`, `readLine`, `readChar`, `readk`, `close`), `FileWriteStream`'s 5 (`fileName`, `toString`, `write` twice, `close`), `Reader`'s 10 (`inputReader`, `fileName`, `eof`, `ready`, `whenUnconsumed`, `consume`, `readLine`, `readChar`, `readk`, `close`). With rung W's 11, P-164's 36 are gone.
3. **At the end of a file every answer stays; a read after `consume` and a missing file now raise the library's exceptions; a read after `close` answers the end's values where it stopped.** By 28 probes under walk, each one operation (`tmp/rung-io-reader/probes/run.sh old|new`, the old code by `old-fortress.sh`): at the end, both `readLine=""`, `readChar=0`, `uncheckedReadChar=-1`, `read(3)=""`, `eof=true`, `ready=false` (and `Reader`'s alike); after `consume`, `readLine`, `readChar`, `read(3)`, a second `consume` and `Reader.whenUnconsumed` stopped with 'Performed operation on consumed FileReadStream …' and now raise `IOFailure`, which a `catch` sees, and print 'IOFailure' where nothing catches; `uncheckedReadLine` after `consume` answers "alpha" on both; a missing file stopped with 'FileNotFound: …' and now raises `FileNotFoundException`, for `FileReadStream`, `Reader` and `FileWriteStream`; after `close`, `readLine`, `read(3)` and `Reader.uncheckedReadLine`, `uncheckedRead(3)` stopped with 'Read IOException on <…>' or '….read(3) IO error.' and now answer `""`, `readChar` and `uncheckedReadChar` answer `char(0)` and -1, and `ready`/`isReady` raise `IOFailure` where they stopped with 'Ready IOException'/'Read IOException'; `FileWriteStream.write` after `close` raises `IOFailure` where it stopped with 'Write IOException on <Write handle to …>'; `eof` after `close` is `true` and a second `close` is quiet on both. Meaning: a program that stopped on walk's error now stops on the exception's name or catches it (fork R6); one that read after `close` now reads the end.
4. **On the compiled path no `catch` sees a raise of `IOFailure` or `FileNotFoundException` by `fileOps` or a `FortressBuffered…` class (NEW-R-1).** `Utility.makeFortressException(name, msg)` looks up `Class.forName(name).getConstructor(new Class[]{ String.class })` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/Utility.java:30`), and `javap -p 'fortress/CompilerBuiltin$IOFailure.class'` from the prelude's jar prints `public fortress.CompilerBuiltin$IOFailure(fortress.CompilerBuiltin$String);`, so the lookup throws and the helper throws `FortressImplementationError`. Holds on the base and on the edit: `compiler_tests/XXXFileOpsRaiseCaughtCompiled` (junit.sh: 'REACHED', 'com.sun.fortress.compiler.runtimeValues.FortressImplementationError: fortress.CompilerBuiltin$IOFailure.<init>(java.lang.String)', 'Saw expected failure (Exit code != 0)'), and the probe `tmp/rung-io-reader/cprobe/CompiledMissingProbe.fss`, `makeJavaBufferedReader` of a missing file in a `try` that catches `FileNotFoundException`: 'FortressImplementationError: fortress.CompilerBuiltin$FileNotFoundException.<init>(java.lang.String)', rc=1, old and new. Walk is not hit: there `Class.forName` finds no class, and `StaticNativeApp.raised` raises the library's object. The no-argument form, which `IntegerOverflow` and `DivisionByZero` take, is not hit. Meaning: until the run time is repaired, a compiled program cannot catch an I/O failure; at N5 the raise strings change, and the constructor lookup must change with them.
5. **A value parameter of an object satisfies an inherited abstract getter of its name under walk.** `FileReadStream(fileName: String, under: JavaBufferedReader) extends { ReadStream, FileStream }` loads and answers `fileName` though `FileStream` declares `getter fileName(): String` abstract (`Library/FileSupport.fss:22-24`); shown by `NativeHelperReaderWalk`'s `r.fileName` and `w.fileName` asserts. The writer rung's `Writer` had no such getter above it.

## For FACTS

**Walk carries `FortressLibrary`'s `JavaBufferedReader` in a Java `FortressBufferedReader`, and `FileReadStream`, `Reader`, `stdIn` and `FileWriteStream` are plain Fortress objects over the two Java-backed traits.** The trait's eight methods and its two factories, over a file name and for standard input, are natives on `nativeHelpers/fileOps` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1959-1979`); walk's loader carries the trait by its name through `FortressBuiltin`'s private native object `JavaBufferedReaderObject` (`interpreter/glue/StaticNativeApp.java:71`). `File` and `Reader` are plain components: each object holds its Java-backed value in its field `under`; `uncheckedReadChar` answers -1 at the end by the reader's `eof`, since `jbrRead` answers 0 there; `FileWriteStream` is a `WriteStream` with its `flush`. A missing file raises `FileNotFoundException` and a read after `consume` `IOFailure`, which a `catch` sees under walk; on the compiled path no `catch` sees them (NEW-R-1). The one library's 428 live bindings: 351 on helpers, 77 on glue classes. Test: `tests/NativeHelperReaderWalk`, `compiler_tests/NativeHelperFamilyReaderCompiled`, `compiler_tests/XXXFileOpsRaiseCaughtCompiled`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-io-reader/REPORT.md`, "What changed and why".

## Changes to existing rows

- Row 926 closes with `14be0d36`, test `NativeHelperReaderWalk`: `File` is no longer a native component, and `FileWriteStream` holds its Java writer in a field.
- Row 900 closes with `14be0d36`, test `NativeHelperReaderWalk`: `FileWriteStream` extends `WriteStream`, so a rope writes itself on it (`Library/File.fss:52`, `:56`).
- Row 901 closes with `14be0d36`, test `NativeHelperReaderWalk`: `FileWriteStream`'s `flush()` (`Library/File.fss:68`).
- Row 902 closes with `14be0d36`, test `NativeHelperReaderWalk`: a missing file raises `FileNotFoundException` through `FileReadStream`, `Reader` and `FileWriteStream`, which a `catch` sees.
- Row 928, its whole new line, for `ledger.py rewrite 928` (linted: `ledger.py check --rows`, no rule broken):

| 928 | under walk, a program's object that extends `JavaBufferedWriter` or `JavaBufferedReader` loads, and its first call of an inherited native method stops, since those are natives over a Java writer or reader and neither trait has a `comprises` clause to name its private native object | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | design limit (library) | silent | none | climb batch 27 rung W's skeptic | siblings: 551. Neither trait (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1948-1968`) has a `comprises` clause, unlike `ZZ32`'s `comprises { Int }`, since their native objects are private to `FortressBuiltin` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:790`, `:795`); the loader's `unbox` refuses any other value (`interpreter/glue/StaticNativeApp.java:296-303`). `object Fake extends JavaBufferedWriter end` with `Fake.write("x")`: 'No Java FortressBufferedWriter carries Fake'; over `JavaBufferedReader`, `Fake.readLine()`: 'No Java FortressBufferedReader carries Fake'; rc=1 each. Workaround: a program's own stream extends `WriteStream` or `ReadStream`. |

- Row 927, a note, for `ledger.py note 927` (the row with it: 1,019 characters, notes 630; linted with the note added): "`jbwWriteChar` is now at `nativeHelpers/fileOps.java:105`, below the new `jbrStdIn`."

## New rows

- NEW-R-1, for the section "11. Parallelism, exceptions and control flow", where a `catch` that sees no exception sits (row 902's section, "10. Strings, maps and printing", is the other place; the gather's choice) (linted: only the number rule fails):

| NEW-R-1 | on the compiled path no `catch` sees a raise of `IOFailure` or `FileNotFoundException` by `fileOps` or a `FortressBuffered…` class: `Utility.makeFortressException(name, msg)` seeks a constructor at `java.lang.String`, which the prelude's class lacks, and the run ends in `FortressImplementationError` | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | implementation gap (runtime) | `basic/expressions/try.tex`, "Try Expressions" | XXXFileOpsRaiseCaughtCompiled | climb batch 28 rung R | siblings: 902. `Class.forName(name).getConstructor(new Class[]{ String.class })` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/Utility.java:30`, at 157323e51); `javap` of `fortress.CompilerBuiltin$IOFailure` shows `IOFailure(fortress.CompilerBuiltin$String)`. A compiled reader's `jbrWhenUnconsumed` after `jbrConsume`: 'FortressImplementationError: fortress.CompilerBuiltin$IOFailure.<init>(java.lang.String)', exit 1; `makeJavaBufferedReader` on a missing file in a `try` that catches `FileNotFoundException`: the same at `FileNotFoundException`, rc=1, on the base and on the edit. Walk is not hit: there the class does not load, and the loader raises the library's object. |

## Handover line

- **R** (`14be0d36`): Rung R landed P-164's reader side on `wip/rung-io-reader`: `JavaBufferedReader`'s eight natives and two factories on `fileOps` (`jbrStdIn` new), walk's carrier through `JavaBufferedReaderObject`, `FileReadStream`, `Reader`, `stdIn` and `FileWriteStream` (now a `WriteStream` with `flush`) plain objects, `File` and `Reader` plain components; 25 glue bindings go, 10 helper bindings come (351 and 77 of 428); rows 900, 901, 902 and 926 close; on the compiled path a `fileOps` raise is no exception a `catch` sees (NEW-R-1, `XXXFileOpsRaiseCaughtCompiled`); count 0 and distance 0 on the final tree, the distance's two crash rows in `Char` as before; `ant testSystem` and `ant testQuick` pass (779; 1,451 + 86 + 263); 52 of 52 demos reach their end.

## Revival change

**The change.** The team's walk library declared `File` and `Reader` as native components whose `FileReadStream`, `FileWriteStream`, `Reader` and `stdIn` are glue objects (base `Library/File.fss:12-81`, `Library/Reader.fss:12-61`): `FileWriteStream` extends only `FileStream` and has no `flush` though its api declares one (base `Library/File.fsi:102`, `:131`), so a rope written to it and its `flush()` stop the run; a missing file, a read after `consume` and a read after `close` stop the run with errors that no `catch` sees ('FileNotFound: …', `interpreter/glue/prim/FileReadStream.java:44`; 'Performed operation on consumed FileReadStream …', `:70`; 'Read IOException on <Read handle to …>', `:79-89`). The tree now declares `object FileReadStream(fileName: String, under: JavaBufferedReader)`, `object FileWriteStream(fileName: String, under: JavaBufferedWriter) extends { FileStream, WriteStream }` and `object Reader(fileName: String, under: JavaBufferedReader)`, each over a Java-backed value in its field, beside one-argument factories of the old names (`Library/File.fsi:17-19`, `:99-101`; `Library/Reader.fsi:17-19`); `FileWriteStream` takes a rope and flushes; a missing file raises `FileNotFoundException`, a read after `consume` and an I/O error `IOFailure`, both of which a `catch` sees under walk; after `close`, reads answer the end's values (`""`, `char(0)`, -1) and `ready` raises `IOFailure`. Shown by `ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelperReaderWalk.fss`. The reason: walk's glue classes take walk's values, so the compiled code cannot call them, and every file a program reads goes through these objects (`explorations/run-c4/src/FlatData.fss:69-86`); the team's own later `FileReadStream` holds a Java reader in a field (`ProjectFortress/BirdyLib/File.fss:20-34`), and the team's helpers already raise the exceptions (`nativeHelpers/fileOps.java:37`, `compiler/runtimeValues/FortressBufferedReader.java:119-121`). The answers after `close` are the team's compiled reader's (`FortressBufferedReader.java:39`, `:56`, `:73`), which returns the end's values once `eof` is set.

**Provenance.** P-164 (option (b) of `explorations/reviews/io-objects-carrier-2026-11-06.md`), with review-queue item 373 for `FileWriteStream`, and forks R1 to R7 of `explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-28.md` at their defaults (R6 for the exceptions, item 384 at its default: they carry no message); climb batch 28, rung R.

## Where the fix belongs, and the precedent search

The map (`explorations/coordinator/map/modules-and-phases.md:441-456`, "B.12 Native code and Java interop") puts walk's binding of a helper in `StaticNativeApp`, which is where a declared type gets its Java carrier (F-299); P-58 gives the binding's form; P-164 gives the shape. The precedent is rung W's writer side, which repaired the same kind of site in `Writer.fss`, both of its objects (`Writer`, `BufferedWriter`); its file has no other site. The sites of the same kind left in the one library: in `File.fss` two (`FileReadStream`, `FileWriteStream`) and in `Reader.fss` one (`Reader`, with `stdIn`), all three repaired here; after this change no I/O object names a glue class, and the native components left are `FlatString`, `Reflect`, `AnyType`, `FortressBuiltin` and `NativeArray` (`grep -ln '^native component' Library/*.fss ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/*.fss`).

The ways the language and the library offer, and the choice:

- A Java-backed value in a field of a plain object, as P-164 takes: chosen, as `Writer` and the team's `BirdyLib` `FileReadStream` do.
- The object keeps one value parameter and fills a field from the name, as `BirdyLib` does (`jbr: JavaBufferedReader = makeJavaBufferedReader(filename)`): then `stdIn` would need an object of its own, since its reader is not opened by a name (fork W2's reasoning in rung W; R7 takes the two-parameter header).
- Each method a `builtinPrimitive` in the object itself, over a helper that takes the object: not taken, since no Java type carries a program object (`interpreter.md`, "Natives") and P-164 puts the natives on the trait.
- The end's -1 by a fourth new helper beside `jbrRead`: not taken (fork R1); by `read(): ZZ32`: not taken, it leaves the prelude's method.
- `FileWriteStream`'s `write(s: String)` as `Writer`'s, `under.write(s)` then `under.flush()`, or inheriting `WriteStream`'s `writes`, `print` and `println`, which flush after each: not taken; the team's own text of `FileWriteStream` already writes through `writeOn` and only lacked `WriteStream` and `flush` (rows 900, 901), so the change keeps its lines and their buffering.

# Rung R, climb batch 28: the record lines

## Findings

1. **The reader side is plain Fortress over a Java-backed `JavaBufferedReader`.** `FortressLibrary`'s `trait JavaBufferedReader` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1959-1968`, `.fsi:1265-1279`) declares the prelude's eight methods (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:592-601`) as public natives on `nativeHelpers/fileOps`: `read(): Char` on `jbrRead`, `readLine` on `jbrReadLine`, `readk(k: ZZ32)` on `jbrReadk`, `eof`, `ready`, `close`, `whenUnconsumed` and `consume` on theirs; the factories `makeJavaBufferedReader(name: FlatString)` on `jbrOpen` and `makeJavaBufferedStdIn()` on the new `fileOps.jbrStdIn` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/fileOps.java:96-99`), a `FortressBufferedReader` over `System.in` in UTF-8 named `<stdin>` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1976-1979`). Walk carries the trait by its name in `FortressBufferedReader` (`interpreter/glue/StaticNativeApp.java:71`, `:104`, `:300-303`, `:327`) through `FortressBuiltin`'s `private object JavaBufferedReaderObject extends JavaBufferedReader` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:793-796`), whose native constructor is the new `interpreter/glue/prim/JavaBufferedReaderObject.java`. `File` and `Reader` are plain components: `object FileReadStream(fileName: String, under: JavaBufferedReader)`, `object FileWriteStream(fileName: String, under: JavaBufferedWriter) extends { FileStream, WriteStream }` (`Library/File.fss:23-45`, `:52-70`) and `object Reader(fileName: String, under: JavaBufferedReader)` (`Library/Reader.fss:24-45`), with `stdIn = Reader("<stdin>", makeJavaBufferedStdIn())` and the one-argument factories, each of which flattens the name by a `typecase` and calls the factory. Holds under walk at the edit `14be0d36`. Evidence: `ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelperReaderWalk.fss` (harness: 'OK (6 tests)' with the four guards), `compiler_tests/NativeHelperFamilyReaderCompiled` (junit.sh: 'OK (6 tests)'). Meaning: no I/O object of the one library names a glue class; P-164's 17 bindings are all on `fileOps`.
2. **The 25 glue bindings of `File` and `Reader` go and 10 helper bindings come: the one library has 428 live bindings, 351 on helpers and 77 on glue classes.** Counted by `tmp/rung-io-reader/count/countbind.py`, comments stripped, the compiler's four files left out: the base build '341 glue 102 total 443' (F-299's and F-32's numbers), the edit 'helper 351 glue 77 total 428'. The 25: `FileReadStream`'s 10 (`fileName`, `toString`, `eof`, `ready`, `whenUnconsumed`, `consume`, `readLine`, `readChar`, `readk`, `close`), `FileWriteStream`'s 5 (`fileName`, `toString`, `write` twice, `close`), `Reader`'s 10 (`inputReader`, `fileName`, `eof`, `ready`, `whenUnconsumed`, `consume`, `readLine`, `readChar`, `readk`, `close`). With rung W's 11, P-164's 36 are gone.
3. **At the end of a file every answer stays; a read after `consume` and a missing file now raise the library's exceptions; a read after `close` answers the end's values where it stopped.** By 28 probes under walk, each one operation (`tmp/rung-io-reader/probes/run.sh old|new`, the old code by `old-fortress.sh`): at the end, both `readLine=""`, `readChar=0`, `uncheckedReadChar=-1`, `read(3)=""`, `eof=true`, `ready=false` (and `Reader`'s alike); after `consume`, `readLine`, `readChar`, `read(3)`, a second `consume` and `Reader.whenUnconsumed` stopped with 'Performed operation on consumed FileReadStream …' and now raise `IOFailure`, which a `catch` sees, and print 'IOFailure' where nothing catches; `uncheckedReadLine` after `consume` answers "alpha" on both; a missing file stopped with 'FileNotFound: …' and now raises `FileNotFoundException`, for `FileReadStream`, `Reader` and `FileWriteStream`; after `close`, `readLine`, `read(3)` and `Reader.uncheckedReadLine`, `uncheckedRead(3)` stopped with 'Read IOException on <…>' or '….read(3) IO error.' and now answer `""`, `readChar` and `uncheckedReadChar` answer `char(0)` and -1, and `ready`/`isReady` raise `IOFailure` where they stopped with 'Ready IOException'/'Read IOException'; `FileWriteStream.write` after `close` raises `IOFailure` where it stopped with 'Write IOException on <Write handle to …>'; `eof` after `close` is `true` and a second `close` is quiet on both. Meaning: a program that stopped on walk's error now stops on the exception's name or catches it (fork R6); one that read after `close` now reads the end.
4. **On the compiled path no `catch` sees a raise of `IOFailure` or `FileNotFoundException` by `fileOps` or a `FortressBuffered…` class (NEW-R-1).** `Utility.makeFortressException(name, msg)` looks up `Class.forName(name).getConstructor(new Class[]{ String.class })` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/Utility.java:30`), and `javap -p 'fortress/CompilerBuiltin$IOFailure.class'` from the prelude's jar prints `public fortress.CompilerBuiltin$IOFailure(fortress.CompilerBuiltin$String);`, so the lookup throws and the helper throws `FortressImplementationError`.
